title: Smart header
notes: A header that shadows once stuck and hides while you read used to need a scroll listener, a sentinel element and a class toggled on every frame. Scroll-state queries let CSS ask whether a sticky element is stuck and which way its scroller last moved.

The sticky bar queries itself for `stuck: top`, while the page queries `scrolled: bottom` to slide it away. Where these queries are missing it stays a plain sticky header, and `:focus-within` keeps it visible for keyboard users.
